name: minimum isolation tier (ADR-020)
description:
Isolation is an ordered ladder, `none < process < container < wasm`, and `isolationBelow` fires when the containment in force for a dispatch is lower on it than the tier named. The comparison is by ladder position, not by string: alphabetically `process` sorts after `container` and `none` after both, so a string comparison would read the two weakest tiers as meeting a container requirement. The `process` and `none` cases below are there to catch exactly that.

Unstated isolation counts as `none`: containment nobody declared is containment nobody can rely on. A request naming no capability never matches, since there is no tool whose containment could be in question.

rules.description: Nothing runs unattended at S4 with less than container isolation.
A tool with no isolation at all needs a human, at any gear.

cases.name: met: container satisfies a container minimum
met: wasm is above container on the ladder
not met: process is below container, though it sorts after it as a string
not met: none is below every tier
not met: unstated isolation is read as none
met: process satisfies a process minimum
unmatched: below container, but at a gear the rule does not govern
unmatched: a request naming no capability has no containment to judge
